name: VPN
author: groot
description: WireGuard VPN control in the bar. Drop a .conf into the inbox, connect from a menu, and toggle a fail-closed nftables kill switch. Works with any WireGuard provider (Surfshark, Mullvad, self-hosted).

barWidget.description: Connect / disconnect WireGuard tunnels, optionally restore the last session (tunnel + kill switch) after a reboot, and toggle a fail-closed kill switch. Left-click opens the panel, right-click toggles the last tunnel.

schema.label: Restore the last session after a reboot
schema.description: On: the tunnel you were connected to comes back by itself and the kill switch stays armed across reboots. Off: every boot starts clean — no tunnel is connected and the kill switch is off, whatever was running when you shut down. Disconnecting a tunnel by hand clears it as the one to restore; the kill switch follows this setting from the moment you change it. Also togglable from the panel.

schema.label: How the tunnel is restored
schema.description: Only used while the option above is on. At boot: NetworkManager brings the tunnel up before anyone logs in and re-establishes it whenever it drops — the only option that covers the gap between power-on and login, but it connects without the roll-back safety net. On login: the widget reconnects it when the shell starts, with the same connectivity check and roll-back a manual connect gets.

schema.label: Show public IP / location
schema.description: After connecting, query an external service to show your apparent IP and city. Turn off for maximum privacy (no third-party request).

schema.label: Public-IP service URL
schema.description: HTTPS endpoint returning JSON with ip / city / country / org fields. Only used when the lookup above is enabled.

schema.label: Keep original .conf files
schema.description: Store a 0600 copy under ~/.local/state so a tunnel can be re-pinned to a fresh endpoint IP without re-uploading. If off, the upload is shredded after import and only NetworkManager keeps the key.
